trial_court: Court of the learned Chief Judicial Magistrate, Srinagar and the learned Principal District & Sessions Judge, Srinagar
case_name: Bashir Ahmad Matoo & Anr. vs State Of Jk Through P/S Khanyar

parties.respondent_defendant: State Of Jk through P/S Khanyar, Srinagar

facts_of_case: Complainant's minor daughter was kidnapped by accused No.1 with connivance of his wife, accused No.2. FIR registered under Sections 363, 366A, 376 and 109 RPC. Investigation ensued.

legal_principles.principle: In cases involving sexual molestation, supposed considerations which have no material effect on the veracity of the prosecution case should not be allowed to throw out an otherwise reliable prosecution case.
legal_principles.held: The inherent bashfulness of the females and the tendency to conceal outrage of sexual aggression are factors which the courts should not overlook.
cited_cases: Rameshwar Kalyan Singh V. State of Rajasthan, AIR 1952 SC 54

legal_principles.principle: The testimony of the victim in such cases is vital and unless there are compelling reasons which necessitate looking for corroboration of her statement, the courts should find no difficulty to act on the testimony of a victim of sexual assault alone to convict an accused.
legal_principles.held: Unless there are compelling reasons which necessitate looking for corroboration of her statement, the courts should find no difficulty to act on the testimony of a victim of sexual assault alone to convict an accused.
cited_cases: Rameshwar Kalyan Singh V. State of Rajasthan, AIR 1952 SC 54

legal_principles.principle: Even though a victim of rape cannot be treated as an accomplice, the evidence of the victim in a rape case is to be treated almost like the evidence of an accomplice requiring corroboration.
legal_principles.held: Hence there must be an indication in the course of the judgment that the judge had this rule in his mind when he prepared the judgment and if in a given case the judge finds that there is no need for such corroboration he should give reasons for dispensing with the necessity for such corroboration.
cited_cases: Rafiqu v. State of U.P., AIR 1981 SC 559
Sheikh Zakir v. State of Bihar, AIR 1983 SC 911

legal_principles.principle: To insist on corroboration except in the rarest of rare cases is to equate a woman who is a victim of the lust of another with an accomplice to a crime and thereby insult her dignity.
legal_principles.held: To insist on corroboration except in the rarest of rare cases is to equate a woman who is a victim of the lust of another with an accomplice to a crime and thereby insult her dignity.
cited_cases: State of Maharashtra v. Chandra Prakash Kewal Chand Jain, AIR 1990 SC 658

outcome.final_order: Case committed to the Court of learned Additional Sessions Judge, Srinagar, for disposal under law.

advising on parental rights and responsibilities
